paper.title: Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases
paper.zh_title: 不确定性下的判断：启发式与偏差
paper.author: Amos Tversky; Daniel Kahneman
paper.description: 代表性、可得性与锚定：直觉怎样节省思考，又怎样制造可预测的错误？
paper.note: 本站双语导读，非原文全文或逐句翻译。原文实验中的数字与条件请在原文中阅读，本页不重构实验结果。
paper.rights: 原论文受版权保护，本页仅提供本站编写的双语导读与来源链接。

blocks.en: The article examines three shortcuts in uncertain judgment: representativeness, availability, and adjustment from an anchor. Each can save effort while introducing predictable errors.
blocks.zh: 文章考察不确定性判断中的三种捷径：代表性、可得性，以及从锚点出发的调整。它们能节省思考，也会带来可预测的错误。

blocks.en: A description may seem representative of a category; an example may come readily to mind; a suggested number may shape an estimate. These cues are not interchangeable with probability evidence.
blocks.zh: 一段描述可能很像某个类别，一个例子可能很容易被想起，一个给出的数字可能影响估计。这些线索并不等同于概率证据。

blocks.en: Try making your own judgment before reading an experiment's discussion. Then identify the information you used and the information you neglected. The original conditions matter.
blocks.zh: 可以先作出自己的判断，再读实验讨论。接着找出自己使用了哪些信息，又忽略了哪些信息。原实验的条件很重要。

blocks.en: Reading question: when does a useful shortcut cease to track the quantity being estimated? This is more informative than simply labeling an answer irrational.
blocks.zh: 阅读时可以追问：一种通常有用的捷径，什么时候不再对应我们正在估计的量？这比简单把某个答案贴上“不理性”的标签更有帮助。
